title: dedicated: improve fleet autoscaler burst controls + utilization reporting (v4)
author: Ethan Kline
description:
Background / motivation:
Previously customers saw noisy autoscaler decisions under transient load spikes: the fleet autoscaler would aggressively provision burst capacity and then rapidly scale down, resulting in oscillation and cost surprises. Existing utilization reporting was too coarse to explain the decisions to SREs and customers.

This PR introduces two coordinated improvements: (1) refined burst budgeting and throttling for Dedicated fleets (configurable burst tokens and decay windows) to limit oscillation, and (2) higher-fidelity utilization reporting and telemetry (per-pool p50/p95/p99 utilization, burst token consumption timeline, and oversubscription events) to make autoscaler decisions auditable.

Summary of changes (single-line):
- autoscaler: new burst token allocator, hysteresis windows, and safety caps
- reporting: new metrics + events emitted to prometheus and event-log, plus fleet-utilization API endpoint
- control plane: new per-fleet config schema + validation and migration path
- rollout: feature-flagged canary + observability dashboards + e2e tests

Key user-facing config keys (defaults shown):
- dedicated.autoscale.burst_capacity_per_node: 10
- dedicated.autoscale.max_burst_tokens_per_fleet: 1000
- dedicated.autoscale.burst_decay_seconds: 3600
- dedicated.autoscale.hysteresis_window_seconds: 120
- dedicated.reporting.utilization_bucket_minutes: 5

Design details:
- Burst token allocator: Each fleet maintains a token bucket that accrues tokens proportional to idle capacity over time. Tokens are consumed when autoscaler attempts to temporarily exceed steady-state capacity to absorb short spikes. We apply a conservative borrowing limit and a decay window so long spikes are not sustained indefinitely.
- Hysteresis and safety caps: Autoscaler now requires sustained utilization beyond the p95 threshold for hysteresis_window_seconds before scaling up, and uses max_burst_tokens_per_fleet to cap transient allocations. This reduces flip-flopping during noisy signals.
- Utilization reporting: Added new metrics: redwood_dedicated_fleet_utilization_p50/p95/p99, redwood_dedicated_burst_tokens_available, redwood_dedicated_burst_tokens_consumed_total, redwood_dedicated_oversubscription_events_total. All metrics are tagged by fleet_id, region, and model_class. A new /fleet/{id}/utilization API aggregates per-minute buckets for the last 48 hours for the console.

Compatibility and migration:
- New config fields are backward compatible; default values preserve previous autoscaler behavior.
- We add a server-side migration to initialize token buckets for existing fleets on first read; migration is non-blocking and idempotent.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for token allocator, hysteresis logic, and config validation added.
- Integration tests simulate bursty traffic patterns and assert no more than 2 rapid consecutive scale ups without sustained utilization.
- End-to-end smoke in staging with canary fleet. Observability dashboards validated in staging and compared to historical telemetry.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag rollout to 10% of fleets for 48h (canary).
2) Monitor redwood_dedicated_oversubscription_events_total and burst token burn rate; if stable, expand to 50% for 72h.
3) Full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics.

Release notes:
- Improved Dedicated autoscaler burst controls to reduce oscillation and cost surprises.
- Added detailed fleet utilization metrics and a fleet utilization API used by the Console.

Related work and tickets: ENG-3421 implements initial autoscaler burst prototype; ENG-5567 tracking reporting and dashboards. SUP-789 customer-reported oscillation incident.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration tests
- [x] Dashboard/alert updates
- [x] Migration added
- [x] Docs/console PR to follow for UI wiring

Squashed commit of the following:
- autoscaler: add burst allocator and hysteresis
- reporting: fleet utilization metrics and API
- control-plane migration for token buckets
- tests and docs
post_merge_actions: Enable feature-flag on 10% of fleets (infra runbook)
Create dashboards for redwood_dedicated_burst_tokens_consumed_total and oversubscription events
release_notes: Improved Dedicated autoscaler burst controls to reduce scaling oscillation; added fleet utilization metrics and a new fleet utilization API endpoint for better observability.
notes_for_ops: Migration is idempotent but may perform short reads on fleet metadata. Ops should monitor control-plane migration job rate and throttle if noisy tenants are observed.
